title: Building a football ownership game in Unity with Codex — mobile UI has been the hard part
author: New_Reporter_7382
selftext:
I'm making Football BOSS Tycoon, an Android game where you run a football club and a separate business that helps fund it. I've used Codex and ChatGPT a lot for the Unity C# work, UI changes and testing. The logo is AI-generated too.

The interesting part for me has been the loop between a real phone and the code. I'll play on my Galaxy S24+, find something that feels clumsy, describe the specific problem, then iterate on a change and check it again on the phone. A pile of passing tests doesn't tell me whether someone new can actually understand the game.

One example: when management panels overlapped, dragging the top panel could scroll the one underneath. Another was the owner's office. I had crammed the next opponent and league position into the top bar, where they were hard to read. Now the office has a little league table showing your club and the teams just above and below it, plus a separate next-opponent panel. The office image shows the current direction.

I'm still working out how much information a management game should show at once. If you've built something similar with AI tools, how do you catch confusing flows before outside playtesters find them?

I'm also looking for Android volunteers for a free closed test. Google review is still pending, so the build isn't available yet. Eight playable countries are temporarily included; ads and purchases are off. If you want to help, email [footballbosstycoon@gmail.com](mailto:footballbosstycoon@gmail.com) with subject 'Closed Android playtest' and your phone model, Android version and Google Play email. Please send the account details privately, not in a comment. I'll add testers and send the joining link once the build is available. Ideally you can stay enrolled at least 14 days, play several sessions and tell me honestly what works or frustrates you. No purchase or positive review is requested.

The 20-second video is a screenshot montage, not continuous gameplay. The office is an Android development capture. The match-summary image is a Unity render of the mobile UI using a synthetic QA match. It's an unfinished game with fictional clubs and competitions.
